title: GOD'S GRACE IN AN IMPERFECT FAMILY LINE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Amram married his father's sister Jochebed, who bore him Aaron and Moses. Amram lived 137 years. The sons of Izhar were Korah, Nepheg and Zikri. The sons of Uzziel were Mishael, Elzaphan and Sithri. Aaron married Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon, and she bore him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. The sons of Korah were Assir, Elkanah and Abiasaph. These were the Korahite clans." - Exodus 6:20-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here at last are the parents whose faith we saw in chapter 2 — Amram and Jochebed, the couple who hid a baby and made a basket. Now we know their names.

But read the rest of the list carefully, because it is sobering. Korah appears here; he would later lead a rebellion against Moses. Nadab and Abihu appear; they would later offer unauthorised fire before the Lord and die. This is not a list of heroes. It is a family with a very mixed record.

Scripture is refreshingly honest about godly families. Faithful parents can have rebellious children. One household can produce both a Moses and a Korah.

If you are grieving over someone in your family who has turned away, take some comfort here. Their choices are their own. You are not the sole author of another person's faith, and your prayers are not wasted.

And here is a beautiful footnote: generations later, the sons of Korah were writing psalms of worship (Ps 84). God's grace can reach a rebel's descendants.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I carrying guilt for someone else's choices?
2. Do I still pray with hope for family members who have walked away?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I bring my family before You — the faithful and the wandering. Do what only You can do in their hearts. Amen.
